sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lens_diagnostics: lens_diagnostics source=session reads the session cache and an empty cache is not proof of a clean file; use source=lsp scope=paths for changed files when cached findings are absent or stale
- symbol_search: Find files by identifier
- effective_config: Explain resolved configuration
- project_report: Orient in a project before choosing a file
- module_report: Outline a source module before reading a body
- read_symbol: Read one symbol's body instead of the whole file
- read_enclosing: Read the enclosing symbol or callback body for a line
- pi_lens_activate_tools: Activate a situational tool
- subagent_gate: Run subagent tasks with bounded retries and a required success quorum
- workspace_session_summaries: Inspect same-CWD session summaries before potentially overlapping repository work
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both
- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.
- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.
- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.
- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.
- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.
- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Ask the user one or more structured questions during execution. Use when you need to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions

4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take

Usage notes:
- Users can type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.

Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. First statement: export const meta = { name: 'short_snake_case', description: 'non-empty description' }. Add phases: [{ title: 'Phase' }] only when the workflow has named phases, and declare only phases it will use. With multiple phases, call phase('Exact Title') before each phase's work or set `phase` in the agent options. Use `await workflow(savedName, childArgs)` to run a saved workflow inline; nesting is limited to one level and shares the parent run's concurrency, agent, and token limits. Optional quality helpers include verify(), judgePanel(), loopUntilDry(), and completenessCheck(). Optional control helpers include retry() and gate(); budget exposes total, spent(), and remaining(), and phase('Name', { budget: N }) sets a phase token limit. The optional `agentType` option selects a named user or project definition that can bind tools, a model, and role instructions; use it only when its name and purpose are provided in context. Its bound model overrides `tier`; an explicit `model` overrides both. Use plain JavaScript only; imports, require(), filesystem modules, Date.now(), Math.random(), and new Date() are unavailable. Use phase('Name'), agent(prompt, opts), parallel(arrayOfFunctions), pipeline(items, ...stages), log(message), args, cwd, process.cwd(), and budget. The workflow must call agent() at least once. parallel() requires functions, not promises, and returns results in input order: await parallel(items.map(item => () => agent(...))). pipeline(items, ...stages) runs stages sequentially for each item while items proceed concurrently; each stage receives (previousValue, originalItem, index).

# Runner config page refinement — Implementation plan

## Goal

Refine the System Settings › Runners configuration screen
(`frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`, backed by
`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, and `runner/daemon.js`)
so that: the whole roster row is clickable; directory fields show effective
defaults instead of blank inputs; model selection toggles runner-advertised
models instead of free text; the operator can re-kick model detection; and the
operator can trigger a runner update from the page — plus the further refinements
in Phase 6.

## Success Criteria

- Clicking anywhere on a roster row (mouse or keyboard) selects that runner;
  selection still works with screen readers and keeps existing test ids.
- Directory fields display the runner's effective folders on first view with no
  typing, and saving is a single explicit save (no double-click confirm dance
  unless a destructive consequence remains).
- Models render as toggles over the union of advertised and allowlisted ids,
  with a way to add an id the runner under-reports and a reset-to-advertised path.
- A "Re-detect models" control asks the runner to re-run discovery and the UI
  reflects the fresh list without a page reload.
- An "Update now" control is offered exactly when an update is available and
  causes an idle runner to update; a busy runner queues safely and the UI shows
  progress/failure.
- `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` pass; new behaviour has committed tests
  beside the existing suites; user-facing docs updated.

## Context and evidence

- Page today: `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`
  (1040 lines, single component). Only the name `<button>` selects
  (lines ~511-520); badges (`updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`, update `failed`)
  are display-only (~556-590); models are a comma-separated text input
  (~854-911); directories default to `''` and the UI states they are "not sent
  to the Runner yet" (~974-978).
- Helpers: `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`
  (`defaultRunnerConfig`, `advertisedModels`, `effectiveModels`,
  `parseModelsInput`, `describeRunnerVersion`, `runRunnerAction`) — pure and
  unit-tested (`runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`).
- API surface: `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js` — list, monitor,
  catalogue, config get/patch, approve/deny/revoke/pause/resume/skip. No
  rediscovery or update-trigger endpoints exist.
- Backend: `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` has no runner-directed command endpoint;
  the heartbeat response already carries a pull channel (`pendingSteers`,
  ~line 279-313, ADR 0011) — the natural pattern for runner-directed commands.
  Badges derive in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` `_public()` from heartbeat
  facts plus `config.runnerMinVersion` / `runnerRecommendedVersion`.
- Runner: `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels`, best-effort,
  12h cadence, `MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`); `runner/daemon.js`
  self-updates idle-only and reports `updateStatus` via heartbeat facts; the
  only forced update today is the 409 `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path.
- Gap: the stage brief cites a grill survey at
  `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/SURVEY.md` plus an idea file,
  but that directory does not exist in this checkout — the survey could not be
  factored in. Decisions below fall back to the task text and code evidence;
  confirm with the survey owner before execution if it surfaces.

## Key Decisions

- D1 — One command channel for both "re-detect" and "update now". Rationale:
  both are backend→runner nudges with the same delivery, ack, and staleness
  problems; the heartbeat pull channel (`pendingSteers`) proves the pattern.
  Alternative (separate ad-hoc endpoints per action) rejected: doubles the
  protocol surface and leaves ack semantics inconsistent.
- D2 — Runner stays authoritative for facts; backend stays authoritative for
  operator intent. Discovery results and effective directories flow runner→backend
  via heartbeat facts; operator intent flows backend→runner via pending commands.
  No direct UI→runner calls (runners may be remote).
- D3 — Directory defaults come from runner-reported facts, not invented
  frontend constants. If the runner cannot report them, the UI labels the
  fields "Runner default (unknown)" rather than guessing paths.
- D4 — Model toggles keep the existing `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
  `{ availableModels }` contract (allowlist replaces advertised; `null` resets).
  UI-only change backed by the same endpoint; no new model-config API.
- D5 — "Update now" respects the idle-only invariant (ADR 0012): the command
  means "update at next idle", never "interrupt a task". The UI must say so.

## Work Plan

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (first; unblock everything)

- Step 0.1 — Survey recovery. Confirm whether SURVEY.md exists outside this
  checkout; if found, reconcile its answers with D1-D5 and amend this plan.
  If not, record the gap as accepted and proceed on task text.
- Step 0.2 — Command-channel spike. Read the heartbeat round-trip end to end
  (`runner/client.js` heartbeat call, daemon heartbeat loop cadence, registry
  `heartbeat()`, `pendingSteers` ack via `steerAck`) and write a short design
  note: `pendingCommands` shape on the record, delivery in the heartbeat
  response, ack path (facts echo vs explicit ack endpoint), TTL/staleness, and
  what a runner that never heartbeats shows in the UI. Output: ADR-style note
  under `docs/adr/` or the task dir; must be reviewed before Phase 3.
- Step 0.3 — Directory-defaults spike. Determine the runner's effective
  master/worktree folders today (daemon `workRoot`, project `cwd` resolution
  in `runner/project.js`, CI workdir logic) and whether they can be reported
  in heartbeat facts. Decide the exact facts keys and backend fallback when an
  old runner does not send them. Output: decision recorded in the Phase 4 spec.

### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (no behaviour change)

- Step 1.1 — Split `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` (~1040 lines) into
  focused units without changing rendered output: `RunnerRoster.jsx` (list),
  `RunnerDetail.jsx` (right panel shell), `RunnerModelsEditor.jsx`,
  `RunnerDirectoriesEditor.jsx`, plus a `useRunnerConfig` hook for
  load/mutate/save/reload state. Keep all existing `data-testid` values.
  Validation: existing `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` passes unmodified.
- Step 1.2 — Extend `runnerConfigHelpers.js` with the pure logic the features
  need (model toggle set-ops over union of advertised+effective; effective
  directory resolution incl. "unknown" state; command-availability predicates
  from record fields), each with unit tests. No network in helpers (keep the
  `runRunnerAction` exception pattern).
- Step 1.3 — Add shared fixtures/factories for runner records (advertised
  models, update badges, directory facts) reused by frontend tests, so later
  phases add cases not scaffolding.

### Phase 2 — Frontend quick wins (existing APIs only)

- Step 2.1 — Whole-row selection. Make the roster `<li>` the interactive
  element (click + Enter/Space, `role="option"`/`aria-selected` in a
  `listbox`, visible focus ring); keep the name button's test id as the
  accessible name. Add keyboard/a11y tests.
- Step 2.2 — Directory defaults display. Show effective folders from
  runner-reported facts (Phase 0.3 keys) as the field values with a
  "Runner default" hint; operator edits override via the existing PATCH.
  Remove or re-scope the double-confirm once the "not sent yet" limitation is
  resolved by Phase 4 (if Phase 4 slips, keep confirm but fix copy).
- Step 2.3 — Model toggles. Replace the text input with checkboxes over
  `union(advertised, effective)`, plus an "add id" field for under-reporting
  runners and the existing Reset control. Same PATCH contract (D4). Keep the
  effective-list summary line. Tests: toggle on/off payloads, custom add,
  reset-to-advertised, empty-advertised state.

### Phase 3 — Backend command channel (the big piece)

- Step 3.1 — Registry: `pendingCommands` per record
  (`requestModelRediscovery`, `requestUpdate`), set via new
  `POST /runners/:id/commands`-style endpoint(s), delivered in the heartbeat
  response, cleared on ack/TTL. Unit tests for set/deliver/ack/expire and for
  unknown-command refusal (mirror the `runRunnerAction` fail-closed style).
- Step 3.2 — Routes + API docs: operator endpoints to enqueue each command,
  returning a status the UI can poll (`queued` / `acked` / `stale` when the
  runner has not heartbeated). Contract tests beside `runnerRoutes.test.js`.
- Step 3.3 — `updateInfoForRunner` surfacing: ensure the record exposes
  everything the buttons need (update available + recommended version +
  last attempt state) — mostly already present; fill gaps found in Phase 0.2.

### Phase 4 — Runner daemon support

- Step 4.1 — Consume heartbeat-response commands: on `requestModelRediscovery`,
  re-run `discoverClaudeModels()` promptly (bypass the 12h gate once) and
  advertise the fresh list on the next heartbeat; on `requestUpdate`, run the
  existing idle-only update path at next idle and report `updateStatus`.
  Never interrupt live work (D5). Tests beside `daemon.test.js` with injected
  fakes (mirror existing `updateDeps` seams).
- Step 4.2 — Report effective directories in heartbeat facts (keys from
  Phase 0.3) so Phase 2.2 has real defaults. Update `modelDiscovery.test.js`
  neighbours only if discovery itself changes (avoid scope creep).

### Phase 5 — Wire the new UI controls

- Step 5.1 — "Re-detect models" button in the models editor (busy + success +
  error states; refresh the record after ack so toggles update without reload).
- Step 5.2 — "Update now" button in the detail header, shown exactly when
  `updateAvailable` (with recommended version in the label/tooltip); disabled
  with explanation while the runner is busy or below-minimum handling applies;
  reflects `updateStatus` progress/failure. Uses the endpoint from Phase 3.2
  via `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`.
- Step 5.3 — Polling/refresh: after enqueue, re-fetch the record on a short
  bounded poll until ack/terminal state; no endless spinners.

### Phase 6 — Own refinements (small, each independently shippable)

- Per-control busy states: replace the global `busyKey` disable-everything
  with per-action pending flags so one save does not freeze the whole panel.
- Stale-runner honesty: when facts are old, badge rows "last seen Xm ago" so
  toggles/commands are read with the right scepticism.
- Empty states: no advertised models / no harnesses guidance already exists —
  extend with "Re-detect" hint linkage.
- Copy pass: remove "not sent to the Runner yet" wording once Phase 4 lands;
  document the idle-only update semantics inline.
- Keyboard/focus audit of the whole section after the split.

## Validation Plan

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
